copy.blurb:
Canada face Bosnia and Herzegovina on Friday, evening UTC kickoff, in FIFA World Cup 2026. This is one of the matches where the model's number disagrees with the closing line on Polymarket — a wide disagreement by the engine's standards on the Bosnia and Herzegovina side, +12.1pp.

The Elo prior reads Canada 1720 vs Bosnia and Herzegovina 1700: 20 points in favour of Canada, which is a meaningful but not decisive prior. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. The adjustment layer is quiet on this fixture — no host bonus, no home-ground correction, no altitude folding in. The Elo numbers above are what the model uses.

Three-way split from the model: Canada to win at 38%, the draw at 29%, and Bosnia and Herzegovina to win at 34%. The away side reads 34% on this distribution — the model's central case for Bosnia and Herzegovina.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Canada to win at 55%, the draw at 24%, and Bosnia and Herzegovina to win at 22%. Polymarket has Bosnia and Herzegovina at 22%, which prices out at American odds of +365; the model has the same side at 34%. The +12.1pp gap across them is the disagreement we're surfacing.

The +3pp Pick threshold isn't on the point estimate, it's on the 5th-percentile from a 100-sample bootstrap of the Elo prior plus bonuses. On Bosnia and Herzegovina, that haircut lands the model at 28%; the market is at 22%. Even on the conservative reading, the gap is +6.6pp. We're not arguing the market is broadly wrong; the closing line and the model are in approximate agreement across recent fixtures by Brier score. The claim is narrower: this side specifically reads mispriced.

The number above is the most recent read; it isn't frozen. With kickoff 24 days out, we're still on weekly refresh; the daily cadence picks up inside T-5d. Injury news, the actual XI, and weather conditions at kickoff all feed back into the prior when they land. We republish on every refresh. The Desk surfaces edge; what to do with that surface is a reader's call.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Bosnia and Herzegovina a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +12.1pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: A +12.1pp gap across model and market on the Bosnia and Herzegovina side. Our Elo prior, after host and altitude adjustments, rates Bosnia and Herzegovina at 34%; Polymarket sits at 22%.
